(Java/1.8.0_161)` via IPs CLOUDFRONT_ORIGIN_FACING\n- O bit-monitoring (`~/scripts/bit-monitoring`) é uma plataforma FastAPI + Next.js 14 + Celery + PostgreSQL/TimescaleDB + Redis\n\n**Objetivo:** Criar módulo `security_events` no bit-monitoring para consolidar e visualizar todos os ataques bloqueados pelos recursos AWS (WAF CloudFront, WAF ALB).\n\n---\n\n## Arquitetura do bit-monitoring (estado atual)\n\n```\nbackend/\n├── app/\n│   ├── models/              # SQLAlchemy (TimescaleDB hypertables)\n│   ├── schemas/             # Pydantic\n│   ├── services/            # Lógica de negócio\n│   ├── providers/aws/       # AWSClientFactory (cloudwatch.py) — USAR SEMPRE\n│   ├── api/v1/endpoints/    # FastAPI endpoints (NÃO app/routers/)\n│   └── notifications/       # 5 canais: email, slack, clickup, twilio, webhook\n├── workers/\n│   ├── celery_app.py        # beat_schedule definido aqui (crontab pattern)\n│   └── tasks/               # 13 módulos Celery periódicos\n└── alembic/                 # Migrações\nfrontend/\n└── src/\n    ├── app/security/        # NOVO — dashboard de ataques\n    └── lib/hooks/           # Hooks SWR (criar useSecurityEvents.ts aqui)\n```\n\n**Padrão de módulo existente:** model → schema → service → Celery task → endpoint (em `api/v1/endpoints/`) → registro em `api/v1/__init__.py` → frontend page\n\n---\n\n## Fontes de dados\n\n| Fonte | Dados disponíveis | Coleta |\n|-------|-------------------|--------|\n| CloudWatch Logs `aws-waf-logs-concertacao` | WAF CloudFront: rule, action, URI, IP, UA (30d retenção, ~165MB) | CloudWatch Logs Insights |\n| CloudWatch Logs `aws-waf-logs-amazonia-alb` | WAF ALB (após habilitar logging no Passo 0) | CloudWatch Logs Insights |\n| CloudWatch Metrics `AWS/WAFV2` | BlockedRequests por WebACL/Rule/Country/BotCategory a cada 1min | GetMetricStatistics |\n\n**Campos WAF validados** (confirmados no waf-report.sh existente):\n- `@timestamp`, `action`, `terminatingRuleId`, `httpRequest.clientIp`, `httpRequest.uri`, `httpRequest.headers`\n- `httpRequest.country` e `httpRequest.httpMethod` — **não verificados**, testar com query de descoberta antes de implementar\n\n---\n\n## Plano de implementação\n\n### Passo 0: Habilitar logging WAF ALB\n\n```bash\nAWS_PROFILE=\"Concertação\" aws logs create-log-group \\\n  --log-group-name \"aws-waf-logs-amazonia-alb\" \\\n  --region sa-east-1\n\nWAF_ALB_ARN=$(AWS_PROFILE=\"Concertação\" aws wafv2 list-web-acls \\\n  --scope REGIONAL --region sa-east-1 \\\n  --query \"WebACLs[?Name=='amazonia-waf'].ARN\" --output text)\n\nACCOUNT_ID=$(AWS_PROFILE=\"Concertação\" aws sts get-caller-identity \\\n  --query Account --output text)\n\nAWS_PROFILE=\"Concertação\" aws wafv2 put-logging-configuration \\\n  --logging-configuration \"{\n    \\\"ResourceArn\\\": \\\"$WAF_ALB_ARN\\\",\n    \\\"LogDestinationConfigs\\\": [\\\"arn:aws:logs:sa-east-1:${ACCOUNT_ID}:log-group:aws-waf-logs-amazonia-alb\\\"]\n  }\" \\\n  --region sa-east-1\n```\n\n**Pré-implementação:** Executar query de descoberta para confirmar campos disponíveis:\n```bash\n# Testar campos disponíveis no log group CloudFront WAF\nAWS_PROFILE=\"Concertação\" aws logs start-query \\\n  --log-group-name \"aws-waf-logs-concertacao\" \\\n  --start-time $(date -d '1 hour ago' +%s) \\\n  --end-time $(date +%s) \\\n  --query-string 'fields @timestamp, action, terminatingRuleId, httpRequest.clientIp, httpRequest.country, httpRequest.httpMethod, httpRequest.uri | filter action=\"BLOCK\" | limit 5' \\\n  --region sa-east-1\n```\n\n### Passo 1: Model SQLAlchemy (`backend/app/models/security_event.py`)\n\n```python\nfrom sqlalchemy import Column, String, Integer, DateTime, Float, Index\nfrom app.core.database import Base  # Padrão do projeto\n\nclass SecurityEvent(Base):\n    __tablename__ = \"security_events\"\n\n    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)\n    timestamp = Column(DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False, index=True)  # index=True obrigatório\n    source = Column(String(32))        # \"waf_cloudfront\" | \"waf_alb\"\n    rule_name = Column(String(128))    # ex: \"RestrictedExtensions\", \"wp_login\"\n    action = Column(String(16))        # \"BLOCK\" | \"COUNT\"\n    country_code = Column(String(2))\n    ip_address = Column(String(45))\n    user_agent = Column(String(512))\n    uri = Column(String(1024))\n    http_method = Column(String(8))\n    status_code = Column(Integer)\n    bot_category = Column(String(64))  # AWS WAF BotCategory (reduz falsos positivos)\n    # IP enrichment (preenchido async via Redis cache)\n    ip_org = Column(String(128))\n    ip_city = Column(String(64))\n    ip_asn = Column(String(64))\n    threat_score = Column(Float)\n```\n\n### Passo 2: Schema Pydantic (`backend/app/schemas/security_event.py`)\n\n```python\nfrom pydantic import BaseModel\nfrom datetime import datetime\n\nclass SecurityEventBase(BaseModel):\n    timestamp: datetime\n    source: str\n    rule_name: str | None\n    action: str\n    country_code: str | None\n    ip_address: str | None\n    user_agent: str | None\n    uri: str | None\n    status_code: int | None\n    bot_category: str | None\n\nclass SecurityEventCreate(SecurityEventBase): pass\nclass SecurityEventRead(SecurityEventBase):\n    id: int\n    ip_org: str | None\n    ip_city: str | None\n    ip_asn: str | None\n    threat_score: float | None\n\nclass AttackSummary(BaseModel):\n    period_hours: int\n    total_blocks: int\n    top_rules: list[dict]         # [{rule, count}]\n    top_countries: list[dict]     # [{country, count}]\n    top_ips: list[dict]           # [{ip, count, org, asn}]\n    top_asns: list[dict]          # [{asn, count}] — rapid threat blocking\n    timeline: list[dict]          # [{hour, count, source}] — via continuous aggregate\n    sources: list[dict]           # [{source, count}]\n```\n\n### Passo 3: IP Enrichment Service (`backend/app/services/ip_enrichment.py`)\n\n**Cache em Redis** (não SQLite — multi-worker safe):\n\n```python\nimport json\nimport httpx\nimport redis\nfrom app.core.config import settings\n\nclass IpEnrichmentService:\n    \"\"\"\n    ip-api.com: 45 req/min free (suficiente: ~230 IPs únicos/dia).\n    Cache: Redis com TTL 7 dias (sem lock contention entre workers Celery).\n    \"\"\"\n    def __init__(self):\n        self.redis = redis.from_url(settings.REDIS_URL)\n        self.cache_ttl = 7 * 86400\n\n    def enrich(self, ip: str) -> dict:\n        cache_key = f\"ip:enrichment:{ip}\"\n        cached = self.redis.get(cache_key)\n        if cached:\n            return json.loads(cached)\n        try:\n            resp = httpx.get(\n                f\"http://ip-api.com/json/{ip}\",\n                params={\"fields\": \"country,countryCode,city,org,as,query\"},\n                timeout=3.0\n            )\n            data = resp.json()\n            self.redis.setex(cache_key, self.cache_ttl, json.dumps(data))\n            return data\n        except Exception:\n            return {}\n\n    def enrich_batch(self, ips: list[str]) -> dict[str, dict]:\n        \"\"\"Enriquece lista respeitando rate limit 45 req/min.\"\"\"\n        results = {}\n        new_ips = [ip for ip in ips if not self.redis.get(f\"ip:enrichment:{ip}\")]\n        # Processar em lotes de 9 IPs a cada 12s para ficar < 45 req/min\n        for i in range(0, len(new_ips), 9):\n            batch = new_ips[i:i+9]\n            for ip in batch:\n                results[ip] = self.enrich(ip)\n            if i + 9 < len(new_ips):\n                import time; time.sleep(12)\n        for ip in ips:\n            if ip not in results:\n                results[ip] = self.enrich(ip)\n        return results\n```\n\n### Passo 4: WAF Collector Service (`backend/app/services/waf_collector.py`)\n\n**Usar `AWSClientFactory`** (não boto3.Session direto):\n\n```python\nfrom app.providers.aws.cloudwatch import AWSClientFactory\nfrom app.models.cloud_account import CloudAccount\n\nclass WafCollectorService:\n    def __init__(self, cloud_account: CloudAccount):\n        self.client_factory = AWSClientFactory(cloud_account)\n        self.region = \"sa-east-1\"\n\n    def query_cloudfront_waf(self, since_timestamp: datetime) -> list[dict]:\n        \"\"\"\n        CloudWatch Logs Insights — watermark cursor (não janela fixa).\n        Só busca eventos NOVOS desde last_processed_timestamp.\n        Campos validados: @timestamp, action, terminatingRuleId,\n                          httpRequest.clientIp, httpRequest.uri, httpRequest.headers\n        Campos a confirmar: httpRequest.country, httpRequest.httpMethod\n        \"\"\"\n        logs_client = self.client_factory.get_client(\"logs\", region=self.region)\n        query = \"\"\"\n        fields @timestamp, action, terminatingRuleId,\n               httpRequest.clientIp, httpRequest.uri,\n               httpRequest.headers.0.value as user_agent\n        | filter action = 'BLOCK'\n        | sort @timestamp asc\n        | limit 10000\n        \"\"\"\n        # CloudWatch Logs Insights é async: start_query → poll until Complete\n        start_ts = int(since_timestamp.timestamp())\n        end_ts = int(datetime.utcnow().timestamp())\n\n        response = logs_client.start_query(\n            logGroupName=\"aws-waf-logs-concertacao\",\n            startTime=start_ts,\n            endTime=end_ts,\n            queryString=query,\n        )\n        query_id = response[\"queryId\"]\n        return self._poll_query(logs_client, query_id)\n\n    def _poll_query(self, client, query_id: str, timeout: int = 60) -> list[dict]:\n        \"\"\"Polls até Complete ou timeout.\"\"\"\n        import time\n        for _ in range(timeout):\n            result = client.get_query_results(queryId=query_id)\n            if result[\"status\"] == \"Complete\":\n                return result[\"results\"]\n            if result[\"status\"] in (\"Failed\", \"Cancelled\"):\n                return []\n            time.sleep(1)\n        return []\n```\n\n### Passo 5: Celery Task (`backend/workers/tasks/waf_collector.py`)\n\n**Watermark cursor** — não reprocessa os mesmos logs 72x:\n\n```python\nfrom celery import shared_task\nfrom sqlalchemy import func\nfrom app.models.security_event import SecurityEvent\nfrom app.services.waf_collector import WafCollectorService\nfrom app.services.ip_enrichment import IpEnrichmentService\nfrom app.core.sync_database import sync_db_session\n\n@shared_task(name=\"workers.tasks.waf_collector.collect_waf_events\")\ndef collect_waf_events():\n    \"\"\"\n    Roda a cada 5 minutos.\n    Watermark: busca desde último timestamp processado (não janela fixa de 6h).\n    Reduz reprocessamento de ~1.300 logs/ciclo para apenas eventos novos.\n    \"\"\"\n    with sync_db_session() as db:\n        collector = WafCollectorService(cloud_account=_get_cloud_account())\n        enricher = IpEnrichmentService()\n\n        # Watermark por source\n        for source, log_group_fn in [\n            (\"waf_cloudfront\", collector.query_cloudfront_waf),\n            (\"waf_alb\", collector.query_alb_waf),\n        ]:\n            last_ts = db.query(func.max(SecurityEvent.timestamp)).filter(\n                SecurityEvent.source == source\n            ).scalar() or (datetime.utcnow() - timedelta(hours=6))\n\n            events = log_group_fn(since_timestamp=last_ts)\n            if not events:\n                continue\n\n            # Parse, enriquecer IPs únicos, inserir novos\n            parsed = _parse_events(events, source)\n            unique_ips = list({e.ip_address for e in parsed if e.ip_address})\n            enrichments = enricher.enrich_batch(unique_ips)\n            for event in parsed:\n                if event.ip_address and event.ip_address in enrichments:\n                    geo = enrichments[event.ip_address]\n                    event.ip_org = geo.get(\"org\")\n                    event.ip_city = geo.get(\"city\")\n                    event.ip_asn = geo.get(\"as\")\n            db.bulk_save_objects(parsed)\n        db.commit()\n\n@shared_task(name=\"workers.tasks.waf_collector.detect_attack_spike\")\ndef detect_attack_spike():\n    \"\"\"\n    Roda a cada 15 minutos.\n    Baseline: média dos últimos 7 dias na mesma janela de 15min.\n    Spike: atual > baseline + 3σ → notifica via SyncAlertService.\n    \"\"\"\n    with sync_db_session() as db:\n        from app.services.alert_service_sync import SyncAlertService\n        from app.models.notification_rule import TriggerType, Severity\n        # ... lógica de spike detection\n        alert_service = SyncAlertService(db)\n        alert_service.trigger_alert(\n            trigger_type=TriggerType.SECURITY_ATTACK,  # Adicionar ao enum\n            severity=Severity.HIGH,\n            title=f\"Attack Spike: {spike_count} bloqueios em 15min\",\n            message=f\"Top rule: {top_rule}. Top country: {top_country}. Top IP: {top_ip}\",\n        )\n```\n\n**Registro no beat_schedule** (`backend/workers/celery_app.py`):\n```python\n# 1. Adicionar ao include list (linha ~12-26):\ninclude=[\n    ...  # tasks existentes\n    \"workers.tasks.waf_collector\",\n]\n\n# 2. Adicionar ao beat_schedule:\n\"collect-waf-events\": {\n    \"task\": \"workers.tasks.waf_collector.collect_waf_events\",\n    \"schedule\": crontab(minute=\"*/5\"),\n},\n\"detect-attack-spike\": {\n    \"task\": \"workers.tasks.waf_collector.detect_attack_spike\",\n    \"schedule\": crontab(minute=\"*/15\"),\n},\n```\n\n### Passo 6: FastAPI Endpoint (`backend/app/api/v1/endpoints/security.py`)\n\n**Padrão correto** — sem prefix no router (adicionado no `__init__.py`):\n\n```python\nfrom fastapi import APIRouter, Query\nrouter = APIRouter()  # SEM prefix aqui\n\n@router.get(\"/summary\")\nasync def get_attack_summary(hours: int = Query(24, ge=1, le=720)):\n    ...\n\n@router.get(\"/events\")\nasync def list_events(hours: int = 24, source: str | None = None,\n                      rule: str | None = None, country: str | None = None,\n                      page: int = 1, page_size: int = 100):\n    ...\n\n@router.get(\"/timeline\")\nasync def get_attack_timeline(hours: int = 24):\n    \"\"\"Consulta continuous aggregate attack_timeline_1h (não raw table).\"\"\"\n    ...\n\n@router.get(\"/top-attackers\")\nasync def get_top_attackers(hours: int = 24, limit: int = 20):\n    ...\n```\n\n**Registro em** `backend/app/api/v1/__init__.py`:\n```python\nfrom app.api.v1.endpoints import security\nrouter.include_router(security.router, prefix=\"/security\", tags=[\"Security\"])\n```\n\n### Passo 7: Migração Alembic\n\n```bash\ncd ~/scripts/bit-monitoring/backend\nalembic revision --autogenerate -m \"add_security_events_table\"\n```\n\n**Editar migration gerada para incluir TimescaleDB:**\n```python\ndef upgrade() -> None:\n    op.create_table(\n        'security_events',\n        sa.Column('id', sa.Integer(), primary_key=True),\n        sa.Column('timestamp', sa.DateTime(timezone=True), nullable=False),\n        sa.Column('source', sa.String(32)),\n        sa.Column('rule_name', sa.String(128)),\n        sa.Column('action', sa.String(16)),\n        sa.Column('country_code', sa.String(2)),\n        sa.Column('ip_address', sa.String(45)),\n        sa.Column('user_agent', sa.String(512)),\n        sa.Column('uri', sa.String(1024)),\n        sa.Column('http_method', sa.String(8)),\n        sa.Column('status_code', sa.Integer()),\n        sa.Column('bot_category', sa.String(64)),\n        sa.Column('ip_org', sa.String(128)),\n        sa.Column('ip_city', sa.String(64)),\n        sa.Column('ip_asn', sa.String(64)),\n        sa.Column('threat_score', sa.Float()),\n    )\n    op.create_index('ix_security_events_timestamp', 'security_events', ['timestamp'])\n    op.create_index('ix_security_events_source_ts', 'security_events', ['source', 'timestamp'])\n    op.create_index('ix_security_events_ip_ts', 'security_events', ['ip_address', 'timestamp'])\n\n    # TimescaleDB hypertable (1 dia por chunk)\n    op.execute(\"SELECT create_hypertable('security_events', 'timestamp', chunk_time_interval => INTERVAL '1 day', if_not_exists => TRUE)\")\n\n    # Compressão automática após 7 dias (economiza ~60% storage)\n    op.execute(\"SELECT add_compression_policy('security_events', INTERVAL '7 days', if_not_exists => true)\")\n\n    # Retenção: 90 dias\n    op.execute(\"SELECT add_retention_policy('security_events', INTERVAL '90 days', if_not_exists => true)\")\n\n    # Continuous aggregate para timeline (frontend consulta esta view, não raw table)\n    op.execute(\"\"\"\n        CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW IF NOT EXISTS attack_timeline_1h\n        WITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS\n        SELECT time_bucket('1 hour', timestamp) AS hour,\n               source, action, count(*) AS block_count\n        FROM security_events\n        GROUP BY hour, source, action\n    \"\"\")\n    op.execute(\"\"\"\n        SELECT add_continuous_aggregate_policy(\n            'attack_timeline_1h',\n            start_offset => INTERVAL '3 hours',\n            end_offset => INTERVAL '0 seconds',\n            schedule_interval => INTERVAL '5 minutes',\n            if_not_exists => true\n        )\n    \"\"\")\n\ndef downgrade() -> None:\n    op.execute(\"DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW IF EXISTS attack_timeline_1h\")\n    op.drop_table('security_events')\n```\n\n### #### 2. **Plan Passo 5: `bulk_save_objects()` does NOT support upsert/dedup**

**Location:** Plan line 309  
**Problem:** The plan calls:

```

This is **standard SQLAlchemy** and does **NOT** handle deduplication or upsert logic. Every call inserts new rows, even duplicates. The plan mentions "inserir novos" but bulk_save_objects always tries to insert.

**How to fix:** The existing codebase pattern (from `daily_aggregation.py` lines 94-134) shows proper dedup:

```python
# Check if exists
existing = db.execute(
    select(SecurityEvent).where(
        and_(
            SecurityEvent.source == source,
            SecurityEvent.timestamp == event.timestamp,
            SecurityEvent.ip_address == event.ip_address,
        )
    )
).scalar_one_or_none()

if not existing:
    db.add(event)  # Only add if new
```

**OR use PostgreSQL insert...on_conflict** (like in `cost_sync.py` line 8):

```python
from sqlalchemy.dialects.postgresql import insert
stmt = insert(SecurityEvent).values(parsed_list)
stmt = stmt.on_conflict_do_nothing()  # Skip duplicates
db.execute(stmt)
```

**Recommendation:** Either add dedup check loop before `db.add()`, or use `insert().on_conflict_do_nothing()` for bulk inserts.

```python
def _parse_events(events: list[dict], source: str) -> list[SecurityEvent]:
    """Parse CloudWatch Logs Insights query results to SecurityEvent model."""
    parsed = []
    for event in events:
        # CloudWatch returns fields as: [{'field': 'timestamp', 'value': '...'}, ...]
        fields = {f['field']: f['value'] for f in event}
        parsed.append(SecurityEvent(
            timestamp=datetime.fromisoformat(fields.get('@timestamp', '')),
            source=source,
            rule_name=fields.get('terminatingRuleId'),
            action=fields.get('action'),
            ip_address=fields.get('httpRequest.clientIp'),
            user_agent=fields.get('user_agent'),
            uri=fields.get('httpRequest.uri'),
            # ... other fields
        ))
    return parsed
```

## Pre-Implementation Review: Passo 7 (Alembic Migration & TimescaleDB)

### Critical Issues Found

I've conducted a thorough analysis of the plan's Passo 7 migration code by:
1. Reading 3 actual production migrations from the codebase
2. Examining `env.py` (uses sync psycopg2 connection pattern)
3. Checking existing TimescaleDB usage (infra_metrics hypertable)
4. Verifying migration patterns and error handling

### Issue #1: Missing Extension Installation (CRITICAL)

**Status:** MUST FIX

The plan's migration at lines 419-444 calls `create_hypertable()` without first ensuring the TimescaleDB extension is installed.

**Evidence:** 
- `/alembic/versions/g7h8i9j0k1l2_add_otel_infra.py` line 25 shows the correct pattern:
  ```python
  op.execute("CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb;")
  ```
- The plan's code (line 419) jumps directly to `create_hypertable()` without this prerequisite.

**Impact:** Migration will **FAIL** with error:
```
ERROR: function create_hypertable(unknown, unknown, ...) does not exist
```

**Fix:**
Add as first statement in `upgrade()`:
```python
def upgrade() -> None:
    # Enable TimescaleDB extension (REQUIRED first)
    op.execute("CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS timescaledb;")
    
    # Then create table...
    op.create_table(...)
```

---

### Issue #2: Incorrect Continuous Aggregate Syntax (CRITICAL)

**Status:** MUST FIX

The plan at lines 428-435 uses invalid TimescaleDB syntax:
```python
op.execute("""
    CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW IF NOT EXISTS attack_timeline_1h
    WITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS
    SELECT time_bucket('1 hour', timestamp) AS hour,
           source, action, count(*) AS block_count
    FROM security_events
    GROUP BY hour, source, action
""")
```

**Problem:** The correct syntax is `WITH (timescaledb.continuous, timescaledb.materialized_only)` and this MUST be a plain view or materialized view, not both in a single CREATE statement. TimescaleDB has two distinct patterns:

1. **Continuous Aggregate** (recommended for time-series):
   ```sql
   CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW attack_timeline_1h
   WITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS
   SELECT time_bucket('1 hour', timestamp) AS hour,
          source, action, count(*) AS block_count
   FROM security_events
   GROUP BY hour, source, action;
   ```
   This works ONLY for aggregations on hypertables.

2. **Hypertable View** (fallback without CA):
   ```sql
   CREATE VIEW attack_timeline_1h AS
   SELECT time_bucket('1 hour', timestamp) AS hour,
          source, action, count(*) AS block_count
   FROM security_events
   GROUP BY hour, source, action;
   ```

The plan's syntax IS valid IF TimescaleDB is installed, but the parentheses wrapping might fail in older PostgreSQL versions (< 13). The correct safe format for Alembic:

**Fix:**
```python
# Continuous aggregate (TimescaleDB >= 1.3.0 required)
op.execute("""
    CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW IF NOT EXISTS attack_timeline_1h
    WITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS
    SELECT time_bucket('1 hour', timestamp) AS hour,
           source, action, count(*) AS block_count
    FROM security_events
    GROUP BY hour, source, action;
""")
```

---

### Issue #3: `add_continuous_aggregate_policy` May Fail Silently (CRITICAL)

**Status:** SHOULD ADD ERROR HANDLING

Lines 436-444 call `add_continuous_aggregate_policy()` without checking if the continuous aggregate actually exists:

```python
op.execute("""
    SELECT add_continuous_aggregate_policy(
        'attack_timeline_1h',
        start_offset => INTERVAL '3 hours',
        end_offset => INTERVAL '0 seconds',
        schedule_interval => INTERVAL '5 minutes',
        if_not_exists => true
    )
""")
```

**Problem:** If `CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW` failed silently (e.g., `if_not_exists => TRUE` in the WHERE clause), this call will still execute but fail because the view doesn't exist. The `if_not_exists` flag only prevents duplicate policy errors, NOT missing view errors.

**Fix — Wrap in try/except:**
```python
def upgrade() -> None:
    # ... create table ...
    
    # Create continuous aggregate
    try:
        op.execute("""
            CREATE MATERIALIZED VIEW IF NOT EXISTS attack_timeline_1h
            WITH (timescaledb.continuous) AS
            SELECT time_bucket('1 hour', timestamp) AS hour,
                   source, action, count(*) AS block_count
            FROM security_events
            GROUP BY hour, source, action;
        """)
    except Exception as e:
        # Log but continue (view may exist from previous migration)
        pass
    
    # Add policy with error handling
    try:
        op.execute("""
            SELECT add_continuous_aggregate_policy(
                'attack_timeline_1h',
                start_offset => INTERVAL '3 hours',
                end_offset => INTERVAL '0 seconds',
                schedule_interval => INTERVAL '5 minutes',
                if_not_exists => true
            )
        """)
    except Exception:
        # Policy may already exist or view doesn't exist
        pass
```

---

### Issue #4: Compression & Retention Policies Unsafe Without Try/Except (MEDIUM)

**Status:** SHOULD ADD

Lines 422 and 425 call TimescaleDB policy functions that assume the hypertable was created:

```python
op.execute("SELECT add_compression_policy('security_events', INTERVAL '7 days', if_not_exists => true)")
op.execute("SELECT add_retention_policy('security_events', INTERVAL '90 days', if_not_exists => true)")
```

**Problem:** If `create_hypertable()` fails (e.g., due to missing extension), these calls will error out. While `if_not_exists => true` prevents duplicate errors, it doesn't prevent "table not a hypertable" errors.

**Evidence:** The existing migration `g7h8i9j0k1l2_add_otel_infra.py` (lines 68-69) calls these WITHOUT try/except, relying on the hypertable being created first. This works because the migration chain is enforced.

**Fix:** Safe approach—keep as-is but add defensive comment:
```python
# Create hypertable FIRST (must succeed before policies)
op.execute("SELECT create_hypertable('security_events', 'timestamp', chunk_time_interval => INTERVAL '1 day', if_not_exists => TRUE)")

# Then add policies (these are safe now that hypertable exists)
op.execute("SELECT add_compression_policy('security_events', INTERVAL '7 days', if_not_exists => true)")
op.execute("SELECT add_retention_policy('security_events', INTERVAL '90 days', if_not_exists => true)")
```

---

### Issue #5: Downgrade Missing Continuous Aggregate Drop (MEDIUM)

**Status:** SHOULD FIX

The downgrade function at line 447 only drops the materialized view, but doesn't handle the continuous aggregate policy:

```python
def downgrade() -> None:
    op.execute("DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW IF EXISTS attack_timeline_1h")
    op.drop_table('security_events')
```

**Problem:** When dropping a continuous aggregate, the policy should be dropped first (good practice, prevents orphaned policies). Also, if compression/retention policies exist, they should be removed.

**Fix:**
```python
def downgrade() -> None:
    # Remove policies before dropping table
    op.execute("""
        SELECT remove_continuous_aggregate_policy(
            'attack_timeline_1h',
            if_exists => true
        )
    """)
    op.execute("""
        SELECT remove_retention_policy(
            'security_events',
            if_exists => true
        )
    """)
    op.execute("""
        SELECT remove_compression_policy(
            'security_events',
            if_exists => true
        )
    """)
    
    # Drop continuous aggregate view
    op.execute("DROP MATERIALIZED VIEW IF EXISTS attack_timeline_1h CASCADE")
    
    # Drop hypertable (automatically removes TimescaleDB metadata)
    op.drop_table('security_events')
```

---
